''' Tech Mo'r ''' was a [[Bith/Legends|Bith]] musician and professional [[Ommni box/Legends|ommni box]] player for the popular [[Jizz/Legends|Jizz]] band known as [[Figrin D'an and the Modal Nodes/Legends|Figrin D'an and the Modal Nodes]]. Along with his band mates, Tech was a registered member of the [[Intergalactic Federation of Musicians]] (IFM) in good standing. Like many Bith, Tech possessed a highly evolved brain, which allowed him a special acuity when it came to analyzing and relating to music. As such, his talents helped to greatly enhance the quality and popularity of the Modal Nodes' music.

==Biography==
[[File:Tech-mor.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Tech Mo'r performing in [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]].]]

Shortly before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], Figrin D'an and the Modal Nodes had entered into an exclusive contract with the [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] crimelord, [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]]. They would routinely perform in the courts at [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Jabba's Palace]] and his [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] [[Desilijic Complex/Legends|townhouse]], but it didn't take long before they all regretted entering into a contract with the Hutt. Recognizing Jabba's penchant for executing underlings that displeased him at a moment's notice, the Modal Nodes began to fear for their lives. It would only be a matter of time before Jabba decided to make a snack of the musicians, by tossing one down into the dungeon abode of his pet [[Rancor/Legends|rancor]]. Fortunately for them, a golden opportunity was fresh at hand.

One of Jabba's rivals, a [[Whiphid/Legends|Whiphid]] named [[Lady/Legends|Lady]] [[Valarian/Legends|Valarian]], offered the band 3,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] to perform at her [[Wedding of Valarian and D'Wopp|wedding]] to the Whiphid hunter, [[D'Wopp]]. Figrin decided that the fast money would enable them to get off of Tatooine and out from under the thumb of Jabba the Hutt. They arrived at the [[Star Chamber Café]] reception hall inside of the [[Lucky Despot]] Hotel & Casino in Mos Eisley.

Jabba learned of the Modal Nodes breach of contract and sent several of his [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] down to the casino to disrupt the festivities. As luck would have it, [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] likewise raided the party and a massive fire-fight broke out. During the confusion, the Modal Nodes met a party guest named [[Wuher/Legends|Wuher]] who showed them a quick way out. Wuher put in a good word for them with [[Chalmun/Legends|Chalmun]]&mdash;a [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] who owned a nearby [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|cantina]] where Wuher tended bar. Chalmun hired the Modal Nodes to play a couple of gigs at his bar, the following evening. They were performing the night when [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] entered the cantina seeking a pilot willing to ferry them to the [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] system.<ref name="Episode IV" /> They continued to perform at Chalmun's on a regular basis. Occasionally, Chalmun's nightshift manager, [[Ackmena/Legends|Ackmena]], would liven the bar's atmosphere by singing along with the Modal Nodes' rhythms.

Shortly after this event, Figrin D'an wagered the band's instruments and equipment on a hand of [[Sabacc/Legends|sabacc]]. He lost the bet, but the Modal Nodes soon convinced him to win their equipment back. He eventually succeeded and the Modal Nodes went on to play the intergalactic circuit.

==Personality and traits==
[[File:TechMor.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Mo'r playing the ommni box]]
Tech Mo'r was one of the more quiet members of the band and was commonly characterized by a "glazed look in his eyes". This was due largely in part to the fact that he was usually inebriated during most of their performances.

During set breaks, Tech Mo'r could usually be found fiddling about, making adjustments on his ommni box.

Tech once lost his ommni box to Figrin D'an over a hand of Sabacc. Figrin never allowed Tech the opportunity to win the instrument back, and because of this, he developed a longstanding hatred of ''Fiery Figrin''. Despite their animosity towards one another however, they still managed to conduct themselves professionally when it came to their craft.

Most of his colleagues in the band similarly lost ownership of their instruments and equipment to Figrin D'an&mdash;the only exception to this was [[Doikk Na'ts/Legends|Doikk Na'ts]], who custom built his own [[Dorenian Beshniquel/Legends|Fizzz]].

==Behind the scenes==
[[Jibralta Merrill]] played the role of Tech Mo'r in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']].<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.sekaimon.com/itemdetail/153566880333?country=US&title=CANTINA+BAND+SIGNED+AUTOGRAPHED+BY+FIVE+11x14+PHOTO+STAR+WARS+RARE+BECKETT+BAS|text=CANTINA+BAND+SIGNED+AUTOGRAPHED+BY+FIVE+11x14+PHOTO+STAR+WARS+RARE+BECKETT+BAS|nobackup=1}}</ref> The artist has never been given screen credit for the role, although later investigations suggest that [[Jon Berg]] was under the mask.

In [[1995]], [[Kenner Products|Kenner]] released a special ''Power of the Force'' series mail-in offer for a five-piece action figure lot containing the members of the Modal Nodes. Tech Mo'r was one of the action figures featured in the set.

In [[1997]], Tech Mo'r was released as a twelve-inch action figure for the [[Wikipedia:Wal-Mart|Wal-Mart]] exclusive Star Wars Collector Series.

In [[2007]], the [[Kenner Products|Kenner]] mold was reissued as part of an exclusive Wal-Mart Commemorative Tin Set containing the members of the Modal Nodes. This time around, Tech Mo'r and the other figures were given fabric vests.
